source: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Air is matter too: a balloon gets bigger when you fill it, and a full ball weighs a little more than a flat one.
Thinking air is "nothing". Air has mass and takes up space, even though we can't see it.
Your chair, a glass of juice and the air you breathe have something in common: they are all matter.
Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. All matter is made of tiny pieces called particles, far too small to see.
Particles in a solid, a liquid and a gas. The particles are always moving, even in a solid.
Is air matter? Blow up a balloon: the air pushes the balloon outward, so the air takes up space. A pumped-up ball weighs a little more than the same ball when it is flat, so air has mass too.
We cannot see air because its particles are spread far apart and are clear. We can feel it as wind, and we see it push a sail or fill a balloon.
Which of these are matter: a rock, milk, the steam over a hot bath, a shadow, a song?
Rock, milk and steam are matter. A shadow and a song are not.
A rock, milk and steam have mass and take up space.
A shadow is only where light is blocked; a song is sound, a kind of energy.
Thinking air is "nothing". Push an upside-down cup straight down into a bowl of water: the air inside keeps most of the water out.
